messages.subject: Re: Statet Graphic device
messages.body_plain:
Hi Benno,

Benno Thoma wrote [2013-08-30 11:33]:
> Hello,
>
> is it possible to open a new page in the implemented graphic device
> directly from a R-script.
> What I want to do: Open more than one page in the R-Script in the
> implemented graphic device.

You are looking for 'dev.new'? The function opens a new default graphic 
device. The default device in the R console in StatET is by default the 
integrated device.
The function to open the integrated device explicitly is 'rj.GD' in the 
'rj.gd' package.

Regards,
Stephan

messages.subject: Re: Help does not work
messages.body_plain:
I have found the solution to this problem:

I did not have the option to index completely because the R config was not
properly set for my *REMOTE* console.

For the help pages to work on a remote console, one should:

1) Run Configurations...
2) Open the R remote console you are using (left column)
3) Tab: R config
4) check button "Selected Configuration", press button "configure"
5) On the new window, on the far right column, the is a button with a black
triangle (near
the button "Add...") : choose Add remote...
6) Choose a name and a directory on your machine.
7) press ok, make sure this is your new R config:

Now the help command work !

Thanks,

Arnaud

messages.subject: R environment index update problem
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I already posted about this issue, that I still experiment.
I'll try to be as clear as possible, and I have an example package on
github to help reproducing the problem.

Description: I can not make statET to index newer installed versions of a
package using "R environment -->  Index changes" action, knowing the
official version string of the package (from the DESCRIPTION file) has not
changed.

Why do I need this ? We work on packages on a daily basis and use
continuous integration.
We can not increase the version number of the package for each
modification. Still, we'd like to have the new content of the help
documentation.

Overview of the example:
I will install a version of package rikiki with FOO1 as description of
entry foo.
Then have statET index this package, and display help(foo).
Then install a newer version of the package with FOO2 as description of
entry foo.
At this point, I can not have statET display the new version of help(foo).

Steps to reproduce:

# get the package
git clone https://github.com/kforner/rikiki.git
# make a temp directory to install the package in
mkdir lib
cd rikiki


# ======= install the version foo1 of the package =================
# run inside statET a R console and set the current directory inside rikiki
# remove the current foo.Rd if any
if (file.exists('man/foo.Rd')) file.remove('man/foo.Rd')
# copy foo.Rd Version 1
file.copy('foo1.Rd', 'man/foo.Rd')
# install the package in temp dir
system("R CMD INSTALL -l ../lib/ .", intern=TRUE)
# put the temp lib dir in the lib paths to that statET can see it
.libPaths(c(.libPaths(), '../lib'))
# load the package
library(rikiki, lib = '../lib')

# ask for help
help(foo)
# nothing AS EXPECTED

Now, in the Console view, select "R environment -->  Index changes"
The indexing process should find the new package, and index it.

help(foo)
# ==> display FOO1 AS EXPECTED

So far so good.

# ======= install the version foo1 of the package =================
# remove the current foo.Rd if any
if (file.exists('man/foo.Rd')) file.remove('man/foo.Rd')
# copy foo.Rd Version 2
file.copy('foo2.Rd', 'man/foo.Rd')
# install the package in temp dir
system("R CMD INSTALL -l ../lib/ .", intern=TRUE)


Now, in the Console view, select "R environment -->  Index changes"
The indexing process does not seem find the new package (too fast).

Now start a NEW StatET R console
library(rikiki, lib = '../lib')
help(foo)
# ==> display FOO1 instead of FOO2

Ultimate check:
*start a standard R console (not statET)*
library(rikiki, lib = '../lib')
help(foo)
# ==> display FOO2 as expected.


Probable cause:
in de.walware.statet.r.internal.core.rhelp.REnvIndexChecker.::checkPackage

I noticed (line 160):
        else if (!packageHelp.getVersion().equals(pkgVersion)) {

meaning that the package is ignored if a same pkgVersion of the package has
already been indexed.

A possible fix would be to store the date of the DESCRIPTION file for
instance, and to compare them.


N.B:
Calling "R environment -->  Index completely" takes ages and crashes:
[WARNING] The R environment index could not be completely updated.
    (details available in Eclipse error log)


Best,
Karl

Hi,

I am running R 3.0.1, Eclipse 4.3.0.v20130605-2000, StatET 
3.3.0.b201306021645E42sw with rj 1.1.0-4 on Ubuntu 12.04 (Unity).

In earlier versions of StatET, typing ctrl+R twice in the script window 
executed the command at cursor position; the combination of ctrl+R and 
ctrl+V did the same but, in addition, pasted the output into the script.

This does not work anymore.

In the Eclipse keybindings dialogue, both bindings still exist, although 
Ctrl+R Ctrl+R is marked "In Windows". Does this mean, this keybinding is 
only possible in Microsoft Windows?

Is there a way to get the former keybindings back in Linux/Ubuntu?

Thanks in advance!

Niklaus
